# Harmo

> A CSS-first UI library for dashboards and applications: native HTML elements styled by `.h<name>` classes, with variants and states as attributes and theming through `--harmo-*` custom properties. Use it as HTML and CSS, or through the React components in `@harmo-ui/react`, which render the same markup; each component page's React section lists their props. Both `@harmo-ui/css` and `@harmo-ui/react` are on npm.

Rules for writing Harmo markup:

- Load `tokens.css` once, then each component's file, or `index.css` for everything. Each component page's Contract table lists the files it needs.
- One class per component, such as `.hbutton`; its parts are `.h<name>-<part>`, such as `.hbutton-label`. Variants and states are attributes, never extra classes: `data-variant="secondary"`, `data-size="small"`, `disabled`, `aria-invalid="true"`.
- Use the native elements shown in each page's Markup (`<button type="button">`, `<a href>`, `<input>`), with the ARIA attributes shown there.
- Ids must be unique on a page, and so must each popup trigger's `anchor-name` (Tooltip reuses one name, scoped to each trigger). Every `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-controls`, `for`, and `popovertarget` must point to an id that exists. A popup trigger's `anchor-name` matches its popup's `position-anchor`.
- The CSS ships no script. Where a Contract's Script row says "Required", HTML without React must keep the listed attributes current itself: Select, Listbox, Popup, Filter Chip, Meter, Password Input, Tabs with panels, and Tooltip (Escape must hide it). The example scripts in `examples/html/src/scripts` show how; the React components do it for you.
- In a form, a Select's trigger is a button and sends nothing: give it `data-name`, give each option a `data-value`, and keep one hidden input per chosen value. A single select with nothing chosen keeps one hidden input with an empty value; a multi-select with nothing chosen has none. Disable the inputs with the trigger.
- Theme by overriding `--harmo-*` tokens on `:root` or a containing element, not by restyling classes. On a containing element, also redeclare tokens built from the ones you change, such as `--harmo-focus-outline`.
- For a brand color, run `npx harmo-ui theme "<hex>"`: it writes `harmo-theme.css`, every role in light and dark mode at WCAG AA, adapted from the nearest accent, and adds it to `harmo.css` when there is one. Prefer it to setting primary colors by hand.
- For another accent color, prefer `data-harmo-accent` on `<html>` or a section over setting colors by hand: `purple` (default), `blue`, `teal`, `green`, `amber`, `red`, `pink`, or `mono` (black, or near-white in dark mode). Each passes WCAG AA in light and dark. `index.css` includes them, and `npx harmo-ui add` copies `accents.css` with `tokens.css`; otherwise load `accents.css` after `tokens.css`. An app's own token values on `:root` win over an accent on `<html>`; to change an accent on a section, override on that section.
- Dark mode: set `color-scheme: dark` on `:root` or a section, or `light dark` to follow the system; without it, Harmo stays light. Token colors are `light-dark()` pairs. A theme for both modes sets each color as a pair, and sets `--harmo-color-primary-fill`, `-fill-hover`, and `-fill-active` for what has white text on it (Button, Switch), since the dark primary is too light for that.

To copy components into a project instead of installing them, run `npx harmo-ui add <component>`. It copies each one to `components/harmo/<component>/`, or `src/components/harmo/<component>/` with a `src` folder, with its styles and what it needs; import `harmo.css` from that folder once. `npx harmo-ui list` lists the components. Copied components import from those files, not `@harmo-ui/react`; everything else below applies to them too.

Rules for using the React components (`@harmo-ui/react`):

- Import the CSS once (`@harmo-ui/css`), then the components. Each component page's React section lists its props; every other prop is the named element's native attribute, and `ref` reaches that element.
- Harmo builds in no text. Pass every word a component shows or announces: Breadcrumb's `aria-label`, Pagination's `aria-label`, `previousLabel` and `nextLabel` (and `pageLabel` with `numbered`), Spinner's label as children, Password Input's `showPasswordLabel` and `hidePasswordLabel` (and `strengthLabel` with `strength`), Filter Chip's `clearLabel` and `formatCount` with `multiple`, and `emptyMessage` with `searchLabel`. TypeScript requires each where it's needed.
- Wrap a form control in `<Field label=…>` for its label, description, Optional marker, and error; Field connects their ids. Pass `error` to every field you validate, even while it's `undefined`, so the error can animate in. Checkbox, Radio, and Switch use `<Field orientation="horizontal">`.
- Choices are children: `<Select>`, `<Listbox>`, and `<FilterChip>` take `<Option value=…>` and `<OptionGroup label=…>`. Selection is `value` or `defaultValue` with `onValueChange`: a string, or an array with `multiple`.
- Set the app's router link and image components once with `<HarmoProvider linkComponent={…} imageComponent={…}>`; Link, Button with `href`, TabLink, and Avatar use them. In the Next.js App Router, do it in a `"use client"` component that wraps the root layout's `children`: passing them directly from a Server Component fails the build.

## Docs

- [Components overview](docs/components/README.md): conventions, which files to load together, and what scripts handle
- [Accordion](docs/components/accordion.md): items that each show or hide their content, such as questions and their answers, one open at a time or several, with no script
- [Avatar](docs/components/avatar.md): a round user image, or a placeholder when there is none
- [Banner](docs/components/banner.md): an inline notice: an icon, a message, and an optional action
- [Breadcrumb](docs/components/breadcrumb.md): a navigation trail ending at the current page
- [Button](docs/components/button.md): an action, as a button or as a link styled like one, or held to confirm one that's hard to undo
- [Card](docs/components/card.md): a frame around a group of content: tinted, raised, or ghost for rows that lead somewhere
- [Checkbox](docs/components/checkbox.md): a native checkbox with Harmo's appearance
- [ChevronToArrow](docs/components/chevron-to-arrow.md): a chevron that turns into an arrow while its link or button is hovered or focused
- [Combobox](docs/components/combobox.md): a text field that filters a list as you type, to pick one or several from it or, with free text, be helped by it
- [Command Menu](docs/components/command-menu.md): places to go and things to do, found by typing: under a search field, or in a dialog
- [Empty State](docs/components/empty-state.md): what shows where there's nothing yet: a list before its first item, a search with no results, or a page you can't see
- [Expand Chevron](docs/components/expand-chevron.md): a chevron that folds from down to up while its control is expanded
- [Field](docs/components/field.md): arranges and connects a label, description, control, and error message
- [Filter Chip](docs/components/filter-chip.md): narrows a list or table: a dashed chip that opens a Popup and shows what's chosen
- [Icons](docs/components/icons.md): SVG icons placed next to text in buttons, links, and breadcrumbs
- [Input](docs/components/input.md): single-line native inputs: text, email, search, tel, url, and similar
- [Kbd](docs/components/kbd.md): a key or shortcut, such as Enter or ⌘K, in text or on a button
- [Link](docs/components/link.md): navigation, inside text or on its own
- [Listbox](docs/components/listbox.md): the option list inside a popup, with groups, search, and multiple selection
- [Meter](docs/components/meter.md): how much of something on a fixed scale, such as password strength
- [Pagination](docs/components/pagination.md): moves through a list shown a page at a time: Previous and Next, and the page numbers if you show them
- [Password Input](docs/components/password.md): a password field with a show/hide toggle and an optional strength meter
- [Dialog](docs/components/dialog.md): a modal window for a task or a decision, opened by a button, code, or a link
- [Drawer](docs/components/drawer.md): a modal panel at the window's edge for a form or details, with an optional preview beside it
- [Popup](docs/components/popup.md): a floating surface for option lists and small panels
- [Radio](docs/components/radio.md): a native radio with Harmo's appearance
- [Search](docs/components/search.md): a field for searching, such as above a list, with an optional clear button
- [Section](docs/components/section.md): a part of a page, such as a group of settings: its title, a description, and actions, over its content
- [Segmented Control](docs/components/segmented.md): one choice from a few options shown side by side
- [Select](docs/components/select.md): a form field that picks one or more options from a list
- [Settings List](docs/components/settings.md): settings with a title, a description, and a control beside or under them
- [Sidebar](docs/components/sidebar.md): an app's navigation down the side: groups of links with icons, collapsing to the icons alone, each named in a tooltip
- [Spinner](docs/components/spinner.md): a loading indicator, sized to match what is loading
- [Stat](docs/components/stat.md): a number to watch, such as tickets today: its label, how it has changed, the number, and a caption, alone or as tiles on a tray
- [Status](docs/components/status.md): what state something is in, such as a ticket or a campaign run
- [Switch](docs/components/switch.md): an on/off switch for settings that apply immediately
- [Tabs](docs/components/tabs.md): switches between sibling pages or panels, with a sliding hover pill and underline
- [Tag](docs/components/tag.md): what something is, such as a ticket tag or "Test run", with an optional remove button
- [Tag List](docs/components/tag-list.md): tags in one row that never wraps, those that fit, then "+N" for the rest, shown on hover and focus
- [TextArea](docs/components/textarea.md): multi-line text that grows as you type
- [Toast](docs/components/toast.md): a short message at the edge of the window that goes away by itself, with an optional action
- [Tooltip](docs/components/tooltip.md): a short description shown on hover and keyboard focus

## Optional

- [README](README.md): status, installation, quick start, and theming
- [Philosophy](docs/philosophy.md): design principles and API guidelines
- [Playground examples](examples/html/src/components): live examples of every component and variation, in HTML

- [SCSS source](packages/css/src): the source of truth for every style
